changelog: Replace C12 to allow cuts after determiners/short prepositions in dense (short‑chunk) settings when they do not detach a head from required complements — addresses the primary finding that the prompt was too conservative and lost short‑latency gains.

Insert after C7 a new principle that treats cuts ending inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses (before the clause‑finishing verb that supplies a qualification/reversal) as very high contra risk — addresses the finding that contra was underestimated for unfinished subordinate/verb‑final clauses.
findings: The prompt underestimates contra risk for prefixes that stop inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses or before a clause‑finishing verb/qualification: it lets cuts that leave an asserted prefix which the remainder then negates or qualifies (contra≈1) survive.

The prompt's warning about determiners/short prepositions is being applied too conservatively in dense (short‑chunk) settings: it discourages early cuts after function words even when short‑latency segmentation requires many small pieces and the split causes only minor cohesion loss.

diagnosis.why: The C12 relaxation made the model more willing to place cuts after determiners/short prepositions, which produced more earlier/single‑word-ish cuts and harmed the smallest latency bins (≤3, ≤5); the inserted C7 rule pushed the model away from cuts that end inside subordinate/verb‑final clauses, which slightly improved mid/longer bins (≤7, ≤10). The two edits offset each other so the net H_set change is near zero but with small harms concentrated in short‑latency settings.
diagnosis.lesson: Respect the binwise tradeoff: keep permissive cuts that help very short latencies only insofar as they don't create isolated verb/auxiliary or other head‑detaching cuts, while retaining the clause‑final protection for true subordinate/verb‑final fragments.
